name: Repair a small tear in clothing
blurb: Two techniques — the ladder stitch for seams and a darn or patch for holes — will rescue most damaged clothes, and can be done invisibly with a little care.
gear: Iron-on interfacing or a scrap of similar fabric
steps: Identify the damage: a split seam, a tear in the body of the fabric, or a worn-through hole. Each needs a different fix.
For a split seam, use a ladder stitch from the right side: small stitches alternating along each folded edge, then pulled tight so the thread disappears.
For a tear, back it with iron-on interfacing or a fabric scrap and stitch across the tear in small, close rows.
For a hole in a knit, darn it: run parallel threads across the hole, then weave perpendicular threads over and under.
Match thread colour carefully and work in good light — this is where invisible repairs are won.
Press the finished repair, which flattens and hides the stitches.
tips: Stabilise first. Sewing a tear closed without backing puckers the fabric and tears again next to the repair.
Work from the wrong side wherever you can.
proof: You repair a real garment and someone has to be told where the damage was.
